# apache — 2005 high-value CVEs (CVSS>=7, CISA KEV, Exploit-DB, or SSVC exploitation active/poc)

Full records for all 25 apache CVEs of 2005 are in `data/cve/vendors/apache/2005.jsonl`.

### CVE-2005-1344
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2005-04-27 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 25624: Apache 1.3.x - HTDigest Realm Command Line Argument Buffer Overflow (1) (remote/unix, 2005-05-06, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 25625: Apache 1.3.x - HTDigest Realm Command Line Argument Buffer Overflow (2) (remote/unix, 2005-05-11, verified=1)

Buffer overflow in htdigest in Apache 2.0.52 may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long realm argument.  NOTE: since htdigest is normally only locally accessible and not setuid or setgid, there are few attack vectors which would lead to an escalation of privileges, unless htdigest is executed from a CGI program.  Therefore this may not be a vulnerability.

Affected:

### CVE-2005-1754
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2006-05-21 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 25702: Sun JavaMail 1.x - Multiple Information Disclosure Vulnerabilities (webapps/java, 2005-05-24, verified=1)

JavaMail API 1.1.3 through 1.3, as used by Apache Tomcat 5.0.16, allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via a full pathname in the argument to the Download parameter.  NOTE: Sun and Apache dispute this issue.  Sun states: "The report makes references to source code and files that do not exist in the mentioned products.

### CVE-2005-3745
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2005-11-22 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 26542: Apache Struts 1.2.7 - Error Response Cross-Site Scripting (remote/multiple, 2005-11-21, verified=1)

Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Apache Struts 1.2.7, and possibly other versions allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via the query string, which is not properly quoted or filtered when the request handler generates an error message.

### CVE-2005-4703
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2006-02-01 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 31551: Apache Tomcat 4.0.3 - Requests Containing MS-DOS Device Names Information Disclosure (remote/multiple, 2005-10-14, verified=1)

Apache Tomcat 4.0.3, when running on Windows, allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information via a request for a file that contains an MS-DOS device name such as lpt9, which leaks the pathname in an error message, as demonstrated by lpt9.xtp using Nikto.
